+**Employee social base.** Pay from the work, except income that is not taxable or is exempt from income tax, and except employer contributions to supplementary pension saving (Act 461/2003 §138(1)). The income-tax exemption does not remove qualifying registered-trainer income from the social base: that income is included before its separate trainer deduction. For an employee's qualifying legal relationship as a trainer entered in the register of natural persons in sport, §138c gives a EUR 300 monthly deduction, limited to that relationship's assessment base if lower. Employer accident and guarantee insurance use the employee base before that deduction (§138(6)); do not reduce those two employer bases by the trainer deduction. A profit share paid to an employee who holds no capital is included. The base is capped at EUR 16,764 a month; employer accident insurance runs on the full pay (§138(10)). For remuneration for 2026 periods, the employee and employer pay social insurance on assessment-base income accounted during sickness, maternity or care leave: the old employee exclusion periods are abolished. If pay is accounted after 31 December 2025 for a period before 1 January 2026 containing the then-excluded days, adjust the base under the law effective through 31 December 2025, as the authority's transition instruction requires (Sociálna poisťovňa, changes from 1 January 2026, item 26). Where someone has several jobs, social contributions run from the highest base down (§138(12)).

-**Employee health base.** The same employment income, with no ceiling (Act 580/2004 §13(1); VšZP, employer page). The employer's 11% runs on the gross before any deductible amount (§13(4), §16(2)(c)). Start with the EUR 45.45 combined minimum only for a full month without excluded days. Under §16a(2), reduce that minimum proportionately for calendar days when the person is self-employed, state-insured under §11(7)/(8), disabled, declared missing, or not an employee. Count each excluded calendar day once. Compare the reduced minimum with the actual employee-plus-employer advance, after the applicable deductible amount; only a positive shortfall increases the employee share (§16a(3)/(4)). An employee with concurrent employers can elect not to apply that shortfall increase and must notify the employer within eight days of the employment/concurrency starting, and within eight days of a change. The employee also communicates excluded-day status where another body is not required to notify it; retain the prescribed written notice (§16a(5)). With EUR 200 pay, no deductible amount and no excluded days, ordinary advances are EUR 10 employee plus EUR 22 employer; the EUR 13.45 shortfall increases the employee advance to EUR 23.45. If the same person is state-insured for the entire month, the minimum reduces to zero: actual advances remain EUR 10 and EUR 22, with no minimum shortfall. State-insured status does not itself erase the contributions on employment ([Health Act §16a](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/580/20260701.html#paragraf-16a)).
+**Employee health base.** Employment income under the health law's own §10b and §13(1), with no ceiling (Act 580/2004; VšZP, employer page). The employer's 11% runs on the gross before any deductible amount (§13(4), §16(2)(c)). Start with the EUR 45.45 combined minimum only for a full month without excluded days. Under §16a(2), reduce that minimum proportionately for calendar days when the person is self-employed, state-insured under §11(7)/(8), disabled, declared missing, or not an employee. Count each excluded calendar day once. Compare the reduced minimum with the actual employee-plus-employer advance, after the applicable deductible amount; only a positive shortfall increases the employee share (§16a(3)/(4)). An employee with concurrent employers can elect not to apply that shortfall increase and must notify the employer within eight days of the employment/concurrency starting, and within eight days of a change. The employee also communicates excluded-day status where another body is not required to notify it; retain the prescribed written notice (§16a(5)). With EUR 200 pay, no deductible amount and no excluded days, ordinary advances are EUR 10 employee plus EUR 22 employer; the EUR 13.45 shortfall increases the employee advance to EUR 23.45. If the same person is state-insured for the entire month, the minimum reduces to zero: actual advances remain EUR 10 and EUR 22, with no minimum shortfall. State-insured status does not itself erase the contributions on employment ([Health Act §16a](https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2004/580/20260701.html#paragraf-16a)).

@@ -65,3 +65,3 @@

 - **Input tax.** A payer deducts tax on purchases used for taxable supplies. There is no deduction for hospitality and entertainment (§ 49(7)(a)). Where purchases serve both taxable and exempt supplies, the deductible share follows the coefficient in § 50.
-- **Passenger cars from 1 January 2026 (§ 85n).** For an M1 car, or an L1e or L3e motorcycle, acquired as a long-term asset, leased on a contract that is not short-term, or for goods and services bought to run one, from 1 January 2026 to 30 June 2028, the payer deducts 50%. Private use then counts as neither a supply of services nor a supply of goods. The cap does not apply to vehicles used only for car rental, paid passenger transport including taxis, driving schools, or as demonstration or courtesy cars (§ 85n(4)). It also does not apply where the vehicle is used only for business and the payer keeps electronic records for each vehicle: VIN, registration number, odometer readings at the start, at each period end and at the end, and a log of every trip with the driver, date and time, business purpose, start and end place and kilometres (§ 85n(5) and (6)). The payer must notify the tax office of a § 85n(4) or (5) use by the return deadline for the period of the first deduction. That notice is not needed for vehicles acquired by 31 December 2025 (§ 85n(9)).
+- **Passenger cars from 1 January 2026 (§ 85n).** For an M1 car, or an L1e or L3e motorcycle, acquired as a long-term asset, leased on a contract that is not short-term, or for goods and services bought to run one, from 1 January 2026 to 30 June 2028, the payer deducts 50%. Private use is not a deemed supply of services under the stated rule. The goods self-supply exclusion applies only to the extent that input VAT on the goods was not deducted (§85n(1)). The cap does not apply to vehicles used only for car rental, paid passenger transport including taxis, driving schools, or as demonstration or courtesy cars (§ 85n(4)). It also does not apply where the vehicle is used only for business and the payer keeps electronic records for each vehicle: VIN, registration number, odometer readings at the start, at each period end and at the end, and a log of every trip with the driver, date and time, business purpose, start and end place and kilometres (§ 85n(5) and (6)). The payer must notify the tax office of a § 85n(4) or (5) use by the return deadline for the period of the first deduction. That notice is not needed for vehicles acquired by 31 December 2025 (§ 85n(9)).
 - **Excess deduction (nadmerny odpocet).** If deductible tax is more than tax due, the excess is first set against the next period's liability. Any part not used is refunded within 30 days of filing the next period's return (§ 79(1)). A monthly payer that has been a payer with an assigned §4/4b/4c/5 VAT number for at least 12 calendar months before the end of the month in which the excess arose can mark the return for the faster refund. In the six calendar months before that month end, aggregate tax/customs arrears and mandatory contribution arrears must not have exceeded EUR 1,000. The refund is then due within 30 days of that period’s return deadline (§79(2) and (3)). Earlier registration or advance allocation of a number without payer status does not start the payer-tenure clock. The refund clock stops while a request to fix the return or control statement is open (§ 79(4)).
